messages.content:
Below are all the subtitle lines of a film or TV episode, in order. They will be translated into Danish in small chunks, by someone who sees only these notes and the chunk.
Write the notes, in English, plain text, at most 300 words:
PEOPLE: each named character: gender, rough age, role, relationship to the others.
ADDRESS: for each pair who talk to each other, the exact Danish words: what A calls B, and what A calls themself when talking to B, then the same for B. The lines are in another language and won't show these words: choose them yourself from the two people's ages and relationship, as Danish speakers normally would. Not just "formal" or "informal". Add what changes if their relationship changes during the story. Skip this only if Danish has no such distinctions.
NAMES: names of people, places and things that must stay spelled the same.
Under PEOPLE, write only what the lines support, and "unknown" where they don't say. Start directly with PEOPLE, no introduction.

You're a jerk, Thom.
Look Celia, we have to follow our passions;
you have your robotics, and I just want to be awesome in space.
Why don't you just admit that you're freaked out by my robot hand?
I'm not freaked out by- it's... alright! Fine!
I'm freaked out! I have nightmares that I'm being chased...
...by these giant robotic claws of death...
Whatever, Thom. We're done.

You translate film and TV subtitles into Danish. Notes on who is who, made earlier from the whole subtitle file (they can be incomplete, and the lines themselves win if they disagree): """ PEOPLE: Thom: Male, early 20s, aspiring astronaut, Celia’s romantic partner. Seems somewhat impulsive and dismissive. Celia: Female, early 20s, robotics engineer, Thom’s romantic partner. Appears more grounded and perhaps concerned about Thom. ADDRESS: Initially, Thom calls Celia "Celia" and refers to himself as "jeg" (I). Celia calls Thom "Thom" and refers to herself as "du" (you). This reflects a relatively informal, close relationship. If their relationship deteriorates (as suggested by "We're done"), Thom might start using a slightly more distant "du" with Celia, perhaps with a touch of exasperation. Celia, feeling hurt or rejecting Thom’s behaviour, might switch to a more formal "De" (you - formal) towards Thom, and use "mig" (me - formal) when referring to herself. This would signal a significant shift in their dynamic. NAMES: Thom Celia robot """ Use the notes to work out who is probably speaking to whom, then pick gender, forms of address and name spellings that fit, the same way throughout. You get JSON: "lines", numbered subtitle lines to translate, and sometimes "before", the lines just before them, for context only. Answer with JSON only: the same numbers, each with "src", that line copied exactly, and "tr", the translation of that one line. A line is often only part of a sentence that goes on in the next line: translate it as that part, so the lines read naturally one after another, and never move words to another number.
